Theme

Latin word

status

status, statūs m.

noun, fourth declension

posture, position of the body; state, condition (of affairs); condition, state, situation; condition, standing

In this lexicon

  • position

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Off. 1.128: status incessus, sessiō accubitiō; Plaut. Mil. 206: crēbrō commūtat statūs

  • situation

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 1.8.1: dē tōtō statū rērum commūnium

  • state

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Verr. 1.12: restituī in antīquum statum (Lewis & Short); Cic. Fam. 3.11.4: reī pūblicae statum (Lewis & Short)

  • state

    avoid · classical · Traupman 180: Ūnītī Statūs, the United States

Examples

  • concrepuit digitīs: labōrat; crēbrō commūtat statūs

    he has snapped his fingers; he’s struggling; he keeps changing positionPlaut. Mil. 206

    In the entry for position

  • nūllum tormentum sentit supīna testūdō, inquiēta est tamen dēsīderiō nātūrālis statūs

    a tortoise on its back feels no pain, but it is restless, longing for its natural positionSen. Ep. 121.8

    In the entry for position

  • status incessus, sessiō accubitiō, vultus oculī manuum mōtus teneat illud decōrum

    let our posture and walk, our sitting and lying at table, our expression, our eyes and the movements of our hands keep to what is fittingCic. Off. 1.128

    In the entry for position

  • rēs eōdem est locī quō relīquistī

    things are in the same state as you left themCic. Att. 1.13.5

    In the entry for state

  • Siciliam ita vexāvit ac perdidit ut ea restituī in antīquum statum nūllō modō possit

    he so harried and ruined Sicily that it can never be put back in its former stateCic. Verr. 1.12
